abstract: Chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by sequencing (ChIP-Seq) is widely used to identify genome-wide protein-chromatin interactions. However, obtaining reliable ChIP-seq data for transcription factors has been challenging for several reasons, including their low abundance, transient or weak DNA binding, and poor antibody performance. Here, we present an improved ChIP-Seq protocol for mapping transcription factor occupancy in embryonic mouse brains. We describe critical steps in tissue preparation, fixation and antigen unmasking steps, and chromatin fragmentation by prolonged sonication, specifically optimized for transcription factors. Our key innovation is the application of antigen retrieval to freshly fixed tissues, a technique commonly used in immunohistochemistry to unmask epitopes masked by fixation, in combination with slow fixation and extensive sonication to enhance ChIP-seq performance. This approach enhances epitope accessibility and expands the range of antibodies suitable for ChIP-seq, providing a robust strategy for mapping the genome-wide occupancy of transcription factors that are otherwise challenging to study using conventional ChIP-seq methods.
